question: A 72-year-old man arrives at the emergency department 30 minutes after developing rapid onset right-sided weakness and decreased sensation on the right side of his body. The patient’s wife also reports that he has had difficulty forming sentences. His wife adds that these symptoms were at their maximum within a few minutes of the incident and began to resolve almost instantaneously. The patient says he had a related episode of painless visual loss in his left eye that resolved after about 10–20 minutes about 3 months ago. His past medical history includes diabetes mellitus type 2 and essential hypertension. The patient reports a 50 pack-year smoking history. His blood pressure is 140/60 mm Hg, and his temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F). Neurological examination is significant for a subtle weakness of the right hand. A noncontrast CT scan of the head is unremarkable, and a carotid Doppler ultrasound shows 10% stenosis of the right internal carotid artery and 50% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery. Which of the following is the expected change in resistance to blood flow through the stenotic artery most likely responsible for this patient’s current symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Stenosis in the internal carotid artery" -> "increased resistance to blood flow" -> "reduced cerebral perfusion" -> "right-sided weakness and sensory loss" -> "expected change in resistance is significant" -> "likely 16 times greater due to the severity of stenosis" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Carotid artery stenosis" -> "increased turbulence and resistance" -> "compromised blood flow to the brain" -> "neurological deficits observed" -> "higher resistance correlates with greater stenosis" -> "expected change in resistance is 8 times greater" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient with carotid artery stenosis" -> "reduced lumen diameter" -> "increased resistance to blood flow" -> "potential for transient ischemic attacks" -> "expected change in resistance could be significant" -> "likely 4 times greater" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Stenosis leads to increased resistance" -> "blood flow dynamics altered" -> "risk of ischemic symptoms" -> "expected change in resistance is unclear" -> "possible 16 times greater" -> 60%
analysis: In the case of a stenotic artery, the resistance to blood flow increases significantly due to the reduced diameter of the vessel. According to the principles of hemodynamics, resistance (R) is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the radius (r) of the vessel (R ∝ 1/r^4). Therefore, if the diameter of the artery is reduced due to stenosis, the resistance can increase dramatically. In this scenario, a 50% reduction in diameter would lead to an increase in resistance by a factor of 16 (2^4 = 16). This aligns with the patient's symptoms of transient ischemic attack (TIA) due to reduced blood flow through the stenotic artery. Thus, the expected change in resistance to blood flow through the stenotic artery is 16 times greater.
